principle.title: Type-First Design
principle.description: Define types before implementation to catch issues early
principle.rule: Always define interfaces/types before creating functions or components
Use strict TypeScript settings to catch all potential issues

principle.title: Dependency Cascade Management
principle.description: When making changes, systematically update all dependent types
principle.rule: Map out type dependencies before making changes
Update from leaf types to root types
Use TypeScript compiler to identify all affected areas

principle.title: Proper Generic Constraints
principle.description: Use generic constraints to maintain type safety while allowing flexibility
principle.rule: Define clear constraints for generic types
Use extends keyword to limit generic types appropriately

before-changes.item: Run npx tsc --noEmit to ensure clean starting state
Identify all files that use the types being changed
Create a list of all dependent types and interfaces
Plan the order of updates (leaf types first)

during-changes.item: Make one type change at a time
Run TypeScript compiler after each change
Update all errors before moving to next change
Use Find All References to ensure complete coverage

after-changes.item: Run full TypeScript compilation: npx tsc --noEmit
Run tests to ensure runtime behavior is correct
Check that all store updates still work correctly
Verify component props are properly typed
Test that event handlers have correct signatures

practice.name: explicit-return-types

practice.reason: Prevents unintended type changes from breaking consumers

practice.name: readonly-for-immutable-data
practice.description: Use readonly for data that shouldn't be mutated

practice.name: branded-types
practice.description: Use branded types for IDs and other primitive values that need distinction

practice.name: exhaustive-type-checking
practice.description: Use never type to ensure exhaustive handling of union types
